changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For ecommerce leads whose checkout is failing, lead with lost orders instead of rates: Stop losing orders at the last step. We'll show you why the card says no on your big baskets, and what we do about it. If you give an uplift figure, calculate it on the customer's own volume as orders and basket value recovered, not as an average improvement in acceptance.
changes.why: The only observed engagement came from Farah's specific explanation of why big-ticket orders fail, while the average uplift slide left the decider seeing 'the same thing'; the champion's own words ('orders dying at the last step', 'the big baskets', 'the card says no') describe lost sales, not authorization rates.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: When a CFO is the decider, especially one who won't take vendor meetings, offer a one-page, customer-specific business case by default: what their failed orders are worth, built from a three-month decline export, next to our price. Give the champion this page to take into the room, not the deck.
changes.why: The champion asked for 'a one-page business case' for a CFO who doesn't take vendor meetings, the SE offered to value the failed orders from an export, and instead the champion got the deck and pricing proposal and presented without us in the room.

changes.change: Counter for when the incumbent bank cuts its rate mid-evaluation: A lower rate on the same declines still loses the same orders. Never let our quote stand alone on a decision page. Show the per-transaction saving next to the value of the orders failing at checkout, in the customer's numbers.
changes.why: After the bank cut its rate, every email became about the rate, and the CFO decided from a side-by-side rate page where our only input was 'Our quote.' With nothing else on the page, he concluded he wouldn't pay more for the same thing.

changes.change: For inbound leads frustrated with their current processor: Your processor can't tell you why orders fail. We can. Open by explaining their failed orders, using the failure rate they bring from their own dashboard.
changes.why: The lead came inbound with her own failure rate (about one in twelve, worse on big baskets) because she couldn't get a straight answer from her processor on why, so the explanation itself was the opening our messaging doesn't name.
